item.title: How do I use the Anomaly Class Bar?: Re: How do I use the Anomaly Class Bar?
item.content:encoded:
Previewing an included component usually won't do much for you because you can't preview changes to the CSS, i.e. the actual formatting and look of the component.

In order to get the look, you need to save the page and it should display.

item.title: How was SCP-5999 Made?: Re: How was SCP-5999 Made?
item.content:encoded:
If you'd like to see how a particular article does something, you can click "+ Options" at the bottom and "Page Source" to view the code.

The code of the terminal layout can be viewed here. It uses an iframe, the contents of which are here and is mostly an HTML block.

Honestly, there isn't really a reason to emulate the article and it seems like more trouble than it's worth. Why are you interested in it?

item.title: Can i post without greenlight?: Re: Can i post without greenlight?
item.content:encoded: Greenlights are required for first time authors to post in the Draft Critique Forum. That being said, there's technically nothing stopping you from posting to the main site without feedback. However, without feedback, you may find that your SCP is quickly downvoted to deletion. I would recommend going through the greenlight process if you want your article to survive on the site.

item.title: Creating MTF's...: Re: Creating MTF's...
item.content:encoded:
do you think it might be a viable idea to have a "reference section" at the end of the tale where these details could be listed?

I'm not entirely convinced that the audience would find such a section interesting, but then I've never been a huge fan of laundry-list material.

If you really want to have a list of reference minutiae, keep it on the side when writing and then ask reviewers if they think it improves the draft to include it. If people don't think it's necessary, leave it out. If people like that sort of thing, include it.
